defect: Absolute or relative deficiency of insulin
keyFeature: Polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, weight loss, and hyperglycemia
basis: Decreased glucose utilization and increased gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis due to lack of insulin action
diagnosis: Fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dl; 2-hr post-load ≥200 mg/dl; or HbA1c ≥6.5%
treatment: Insulin (mandatory Type 1); oral hypoglycemics (Type 2); diet and exercise

keyFeature: Coma, fruity/sweet breath (acetone), and Kussmaul breathing
basis: Excessive fatty acid mobilisation and oxidation accumulates ketone bodies (acetoacetate, β-OH-butyrate, acetone) causing metabolic acidosis
diagnosis: Glucose >250 mg/dl; blood pH <7.3; positive Rothera's test for ketonuria
treatment: Insulin, IV fluids, strict potassium monitoring

defect: Insulin overdose, insulinoma, or enzymatic blocks in glucose production
keyFeature: Tremors, seizures, cyanosis, and loss of consciousness
basis: Plasma glucose falls below 50 mg/dl; brain deprived of its primary fuel
diagnosis: Random plasma glucose <50 mg/dl
treatment: Immediate oral or IV glucose

keyFeature: Hepatomegaly, jaundice, bilateral cataract, and mental retardation
basis: Accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate damages liver; galactitol in lens causes osmotic swelling and cataract
diagnosis: Absent RBC GALT activity; positive Benedict's test (reducing sugar) with negative glucose-specific test
treatment: Strict lactose and galactose-free diet

keyFeature: Congenital cataract; milder than classic galactosemia
basis: Failure to phosphorylate galactose → high galactose reduced to galactitol in the lens
diagnosis: Galactose in blood/urine; low RBC galactokinase activity
treatment: Lactose- and galactose-free diet

keyFeature: Postprandial hypoglycemia, vomiting, jaundice, and hepatomegaly after fruit or sucrose intake
basis: Accumulated fructose-1-phosphate inhibits glycogen phosphorylase and sequesters Pi, hampering ATP production
diagnosis: Fructose in urine; positive Seliwanoff's test
treatment: Complete removal of sucrose, fructose, and sorbitol from diet

keyFeature: Asymptomatic; detected accidentally
basis: Fructose not metabolised in liver; excreted in urine
diagnosis: Positive Benedict's and Seliwanoff's tests in urine without clinical symptoms
treatment: No treatment required (benign)

keyFeature: Abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, and flatulence after dairy
basis: Undigested lactose is osmotically active and fermented by bacteria into SCFAs and gases (CO₂, H₂, CHÃ¢ÂÂ)
diagnosis: Breath hydrogen test (rise >20 ppm); stool pH <5.5
treatment: Lactose-free diet or commercial lactase preparations

keyFeature: Fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis
basis: Block in rate-limiting step of gluconeogenesis prevents synthesis of glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors
diagnosis: Hypoglycemia with increased pyruvate and normal lactate/pyruvate ratio
treatment: Frequent feeding; avoidance of prolonged fasting

keyFeature: Asymptomatic - benign condition
basis: Failure to convert L-xylulose to D-xylulose → excretion in urine
diagnosis: Positive Benedict's and Bial's tests (green colour) in urine
treatment: No treatment required

keyFeature: Profound fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and 'doll-like face' with fatty cheeks
basis: Liver cannot release free glucose from G6P → glycogen accumulation; G6P shunted to lactic acid and uric acid
diagnosis: High blood lactate/uric acid; G6Pase gene mutation analysis; liver biopsy
treatment: Frequent feeding with glucose or uncooked corn starch; allopurinol for hyperuricemia

keyFeature: Massive cardiomegaly, severe hypotonia ('floppy infant'), and cardiac failure
basis: Glycogen accumulates within lysosomes of virtually every tissue, especially heart and skeletal muscle
diagnosis: Enzyme assay (acid maltase) in WBC, fibroblasts, or dried blood spot; muscle biopsy
treatment: Recombinant enzyme replacement therapy (α-glucosidase)

keyFeature: Fasting hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, and muscle weakness (myopathy)
basis: Glycogen broken down only to 'limit dextrin' but no further → accumulation
diagnosis: Glucagon challenge test (glucose rises postprandially but not when fasting); liver histology
treatment: High-protein diet and frequent small meals with snacks

keyFeature: Hepatosplenomegaly, progressive liver cirrhosis, and early death
basis: Synthesis of insoluble, abnormal amylopectin-like glycogen (very few branches) triggers fibrotic reactions
diagnosis: Enzyme assay in liver or fibroblasts; liver biopsy
treatment: Liver transplantation is often the only definitive option

keyFeature: Exercise intolerance, muscle cramps, myoglobinuria, and 'second wind' phenomenon
basis: Inability to break down muscle glycogen prevents supply of glucose-1-P for ATP during exercise
diagnosis: Ischemic exercise test (blood lactate fails to rise); muscle biopsy showing high glycogen
treatment: Dietary modification (pre-exercise glucose) and moderate aerobic exercise

keyFeature: Hepatomegaly and mild fasting hypoglycemia; generally good prognosis
basis: Impaired release of glucose from liver glycogen during fasting
diagnosis: Enzyme assay in liver or blood cells
treatment: Frequent small meals to prevent hypoglycemia

keyFeature: Exercise intolerance (similar to Type V) and hemolytic anemia
basis: Lack of PFK-1 prevents use of glucose for energy in muscles and shortens RBC lifespan
diagnosis: Muscle biopsy showing high glycogen; RBC PFK enzyme assay
treatment: Avoidance of high-intensity exercise

keyFeature: Mild exercise intolerance; generally good prognosis
basis: Deficiency in the enzyme complex that activates glycogen phosphorylase in muscle
diagnosis: Enzyme assay in muscle tissue
treatment: Dietary management if symptomatic; often no specific treatment required

defect: LDL receptor defect or Apo B-100 mutation
keyFeature: Tuberous or tendon xanthomas, early atherosclerosis, and high risk of CAD
basis: Impaired clearance of LDL from plasma results in very high circulating cholesterol
diagnosis: Total cholesterol >240 mg/dl; LDL >190 mg/dl; clinical xanthomas
treatment: Statins (e.g., lovastatin); low cholesterol/saturated fat diet; increased PUFA intake

defect: VLDL overproduction (Type IV) or Apo A-V defect (Type V)
keyFeature: Eruptive xanthomas, abdominal pain, and risk of acute pancreatitis
basis: Excessive hepatic VLDL secretion or secondary causes (alcohol, diabetes) increase circulating TAGs
diagnosis: Fasting serum triglycerides >200 mg/dl; high VLDL
treatment: Weight reduction; restrict alcohol and refined carbohydrates; fibrates

defect: Combined LDL receptor defect and VLDL overproduction (IIb) or Apo E defect (Type III)
keyFeature: Palmar xanthomas (Type III), tuberous xanthomas, and premature vascular disease
basis: Impaired clearance of both LDL and lipoprotein remnants (chylomicron and VLDL remnants)
diagnosis: Elevation of both cholesterol and TAG; 'broad beta' band on electrophoresis (Type III)
treatment: Weight reduction; restrict fat/cholesterol; statins

keyFeature: Malabsorption, acanthocytosis (spiny RBCs), and retinitis pigmentosa
basis: Failure to assemble Apo B-containing lipoproteins (chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL)
diagnosis: Absent beta-lipoprotein band on electrophoresis; near-absent serum TAG and cholesterol
treatment: Low-fat diet; massive oral doses of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)

keyFeature: Large orange-yellow tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, and recurrent peripheral neuropathy
basis: Absent transporter prevents cholesterol efflux from cells to HDL → tissue deposits and very low plasma HDL
diagnosis: Near-absent plasma HDL and Apo A1
treatment: Management of cardiovascular risk

defect: Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) or Apo C-II activator deficiency
keyFeature: Milky plasma, eruptive xanthomas, hepatomegaly, and acute pancreatitis
basis: Inability to hydrolyse TAGs in chylomicrons and VLDL leads to massive accumulation
diagnosis: Creamy plasma layer; TAG >1000 mg/dl; low/absent LPL activity
treatment: Strict fat restriction; MCT supplementation

defect: Deficiency of carnitine or its translocase system
keyFeature: Muscle cramps, exercise intolerance, and non-ketotic hypoglycemia
basis: Impaired transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria prevents β-oxidation
diagnosis: Low plasma carnitine; increased acylcarnitine levels
treatment: Dietary carnitine supplementation

keyFeature: SIDS, profound hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting, and coma
basis: Inability to oxidise medium-chain fatty acids (6-12C) for fuel during fasting → hypoketotic hypoglycemia
diagnosis: Acylcarnitine profile (elevated octanoylcarnitine C8); suberylglycine in urine
treatment: Avoidance of fasting; frequent high-carbohydrate meals; emergency glucose

defect: PEX gene mutations → peroxisome biogenesis defect
keyFeature: Cerebrohepatorenal syndrome, severe hypotonia, liver failure, and early death
basis: Lack of functional peroxisomes causes accumulation of VLCFA and deficiency of plasmalogens
diagnosis: Raised plasma VLCFA (cerotic acid C26:0); low glycerol-ether lipids
treatment: Symptomatic only; prognosis very poor

keyFeature: Night blindness (retinitis pigmentosa), sensorineural deafness, cerebellar ataxia, and neuropathy
basis: Accumulation of dietary phytanic acid in tissues because the first step of its oxidation is blocked
diagnosis: Markedly elevated phytanic acid in plasma
treatment: Strict restriction of phytanic acid (avoid milk, dairy, animal fats)

pathway: Lipoprotein metabolism and reverse cholesterol transport
keyFeature: HDL is incapable of effectively taking cholesterol from peripheral tissues to the liver
basis: LCAT esterifies free cholesterol on HDL; without it, cholesterol excretion is reduced, potentially leading to lipid accumulation in tissues
diagnosis: Abnormal lipid profile with impaired HDL cholesterol transport capacity
treatment: Specific treatment options not well established

keyFeature: Mental retardation, hypopigmentation (fair skin/blue eyes), and mousy body odour
basis: High phenylalanine shunted to alternative pathways producing neurotoxic phenyl ketones (e.g., phenylacetate)
diagnosis: Blood Phe >20 mg/dl; Guthrie test; urine ferric chloride test (blue-green colour)
treatment: Lifelong low-phenylalanine diet and tyrosine supplementation

keyFeature: Cabbage-like odour, liver failure, renal tubular damage, and failure to thrive
basis: Accumulation of succinylacetone - highly toxic to hepatocytes and renal cells
diagnosis: Succinylacetone in urine; elevated plasma tyrosine and methionine
treatment: Nitisinone (NTBC); low Phe/Tyr diet

keyFeature: Dendritic corneal ulcers and palmoplantar keratosis
basis: Markedly high tyrosine crystallises and causes inflammation in the eye and skin
diagnosis: Markedly raised tyrosine in blood and urine
treatment: Strict dietary restriction of tyrosine and phenylalanine

keyFeature: Neurological abnormalities; can be transient in newborns
basis: Block in conversion of pHPPA to homogentisic acid
diagnosis: pHPPA and hydroxyphenyl lactic acid in urine
treatment: Ascorbic acid supplementation and mild protein restriction

keyFeature: Urine turns black on standing; ochronosis (black cartilage/ear); and severe arthritis
basis: Homogentisic acid (HGA) accumulates and polymerises into black 'alkaptone' pigments deposited in tissues
diagnosis: Positive silver nitrate or ferric chloride (transient blue) in urine; HGA detection
treatment: Low protein diet (restricting Phe/Tyr); high-dose Vitamin C

keyFeature: Burnt sugar urine odour, poor feeding, seizures, and progressive neurodegeneration
basis: Accumulation of BCAAs and α-ketoacids; leucine is particularly neurotoxic
diagnosis: Elevated BCAAs on tandem mass spectrometry; positive DNPH test (yellow precipitate) in urine
treatment: Diet restricting BCAAs; high-dose thiamine in thiamine-responsive variants

pathway: Methionine and sulfur amino acid metabolism
keyFeature: Ectopia lentis (lens dislocation), tall stature, mental retardation, and high risk of thrombosis
basis: Excess homocysteine interferes with collagen cross-linking and damages vascular endothelium
diagnosis: High serum homocysteine and methionine; positive cyanide-nitroprusside test
treatment: High-dose Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine); low-methionine diet; B12 and folate

pathway: Amino acid transport in intestine and renal tubules
keyFeature: Pellagra-like skin rash, cerebellar ataxia, and psychotic behaviour
basis: Defective reabsorption of tryptophan leads to secondary niacin deficiency
diagnosis: Neutral aminoaciduria; indican in urine (Obermeyer test)
treatment: High-protein diet and nicotinamide (niacin) supplementation

defect: Defective renal/intestinal transporter for COLA (Cystine, Ornithine, Lysine, Arginine)
keyFeature: Recurrent cystine kidney stones
basis: Failure to reabsorb cystine → low solubility in urine → stone formation
diagnosis: Hexagonal crystals in urine microscopy; positive cyanide-nitroprusside test
treatment: Massive fluid intake and alkalinisation of urine

keyFeature: Speech defects and mild mental retardation
basis: Inability to convert histidine to urocanic acid → elevated histidine in blood and urine
diagnosis: High serum histidine; positive ferric chloride test (grey-green colour)
treatment: Dietary histidine restriction if symptomatic

keyFeature: Cystine crystal deposition in organs (liver, cornea, kidney) and renal failure
basis: Intra-lysosomal accumulation of cystine across multiple tissues
diagnosis: Cystine crystals in WBCs or bone marrow/liver biopsy
treatment: High fluid intake, alkalinisation, and cysteamine therapy

defect: Localized patchy absence of melanin from the skin
pathway: Melanin synthesis pathway (tyrosine to melanin via tyrosinase)
keyFeature: Depigmented white patches on skin, often progressing rapidly over months
basis: Autoimmune disorder where autoantibodies destroy melanoblasts in regional areas, preventing melanin synthesis
diagnosis: Clinical presentation of white patches; distinguished from albinism (generalized vs patchy lack of tyrosinase)
treatment: Psoralens + UV light irradiation (PUVA therapy); consistent use of sunscreens

defect: Defect in the glycine cleavage system
keyFeature: Inborn error of amino acid metabolism with excess glycine
basis: Defective glycine cleavage system leads to accumulation of glycine
diagnosis: Measurement of amino acid levels in plasma and urine showing excess glycine
treatment: Specific treatment protocols not well established

keyFeature: Severe hyperammonemia, vomiting, lethargy, and mental retardation
basis: Deficiency of the first and rate-limiting step of the urea cycle → massive accumulation of ammonia toxic to the brain
diagnosis: Very high NHÃ¢ÂÂ in blood; detected on neonatal tandem mass spectrometry
treatment: Low-protein diet; frequent feeds; ammonia scavengers (sodium benzoate, sodium phenylacetate)

keyFeature: Hyperammonemia, aversion to protein-rich food, mental retardation, and orotic aciduria
basis: Accumulated carbamoyl phosphate shunts to cytosol → enters pyrimidine pathway → excess orotic acid
diagnosis: High blood ammonia; low citrulline; markedly raised urinary orotic acid
treatment: Low-protein diet; citrulline or arginine supplementation; sodium benzoate

keyFeature: Hyperammonemia, vomiting, seizures, and potential liver failure
basis: Block converting citrulline + aspartate to argininosuccinate → citrulline accumulates in blood and CSF
diagnosis: High blood citrulline and ammonia; citrullinuria (1-2 g/day)
treatment: Low-protein diet; avoid breast milk (citrulline content); ammonia scavengers

keyFeature: Hyperammonemia and trichorrhexis nodosa (friable, tufted brittle hair)
basis: Failure to split argininosuccinate into arginine and fumarate → accumulation in blood, CSF, and urine
diagnosis: Argininosuccinate identified in urine and blood; raised ammonia
treatment: Low-protein diet; arginine supplementation

keyFeature: Spastic tetraparesis/diplegia, microcephaly, and low IQ
basis: Final step of urea cycle blocked → accumulation of arginine in blood and CSF
diagnosis: Elevated arginine in blood; excretion of cystine and lysine in urine
treatment: Low-protein diet; arginine supplementation restricted

defect: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase or deficiency of adenosyl-B12 co-enzyme
pathway: Catabolism of BCAAs and odd-chain fatty acids
keyFeature: Ketoacidosis, hypotonia, and severe mental/physical retardation
basis: Failure to convert methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA → neurotoxic methylmalonic acid accumulates
diagnosis: Marked elevation of methylmalonic acid in blood and urine; metabolic acidosis
treatment: Low-protein diet; pharmacological doses of Vitamin B12 (if B12 processing defect)

keyFeature: Ketoacidosis, vomiting, lethargy, and hypotonia
basis: Block in conversion of propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA → toxic propionate accumulation
diagnosis: Propionic acid in organic acid analysis; increased lactate
treatment: Dietary protein restriction and cofactor therapy

keyFeature: Characteristic 'sweaty feet' or cheesy odour of urine and body fluids
basis: Accumulation of isovaleryl-CoA → formation and excretion of toxic isovaleric acid
diagnosis: GC-MS showing 3-hydroxy-isovaleric acid; positive DNPH test (yellow precipitate)
treatment: Supportive care; low-protein diet specifically restricting leucine

keyFeature: Progressive neurological defects, cerebral palsy, and convulsions
basis: Failure to oxidise glutaryl-CoA → glutaric acid accumulates in tissues and urine
diagnosis: Glutaric acid identified in urinary organic acid profile
treatment: Dietary management and supportive care

defect: Overproduction of uric acid (PRPP synthetase activity) or underexcretion by kidneys
keyFeature: Excruciating pain in big toe, tophi (urate crystals), and acute arthritis
basis: Deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals in joints and synovial fluid due to hyperuricemia
diagnosis: Serum uric acid >7 mg/dl; needle-shaped negatively birefringent MSU crystals in synovial fluid
treatment: Allopurinol (xanthine oxidase inhibitor); colchicine; NSAIDs

keyFeature: Self-mutilation (biting lips and fingers), spasticity, and mental retardation
basis: Deficiency prevents purine salvage → PRPP accumulates → excessive uric acid production
diagnosis: High serum uric acid (9-11 mg/dl); orangish sand (urates) in child's diaper
treatment: Allopurinol to lower uric acid; management of neurological/behavioural symptoms

keyFeature: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) with recurrent infections; absent T and B cell function
basis: Accumulation of dATP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase → prevents DNA synthesis → lymphocyte death
diagnosis: Reduced lymphocyte counts; ADA enzyme assay; hypouricemia
treatment: Gene therapy; bone marrow transplant; periodic injections of bovine ADA

keyFeature: Hypouricemia and possible kidney stones; often asymptomatic
basis: Block in conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid
diagnosis: Extremely low serum uric acid; increased urinary hypoxanthine and xanthine
treatment: Low-purine diet and high fluid intake to prevent stones

defect: OPRTase (orotate phosphoribosyl transferase) and OMP decarboxylase
keyFeature: Megaloblastic anemia (unresponsive to B12/folate) and retarded growth
basis: Block in pyrimidine synthesis prevents feedback inhibition → excessive orotic acid production and crystal formation
diagnosis: Orotate crystals in urine; megaloblastic changes in blood
treatment: Feeding cytidine or uridine to bypass the block and restore UTP feedback

keyFeature: Acute abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and NO photosensitivity
basis: ALA and PBG accumulate and act as neurotoxins
diagnosis: Fresh urine colourless but turns dark/purple on standing; positive Watson-Schwartz test for PBG
treatment: High carbohydrate diet; heme arginate/hematin; strictly avoid barbiturates and porphyrinogenic drugs

keyFeature: Photosensitivity, red erythematous itchy lesions, and skin blistering/scarring
basis: Uroporphyrins accumulate in skin and generate free radicals on UV light exposure
diagnosis: High urinary uroporphyrins; urine peak absorption at 405 nm (Soret band)
treatment: Avoidance of sunlight; phlebotomy to reduce iron stores; low-dose chloroquine

keyFeature: Extreme photosensitivity, dark red 'port wine' urine, and erythrodontia (teeth fluoresce red under UV)
basis: Excessive formation of Type I porphyrin isomers - useless for heme synthesis and highly damaging to skin on light exposure
diagnosis: Markedly high uroporphyrin I and coproporphyrin I in urine and feces
treatment: Total avoidance of sunlight; management of skin complications

keyFeature: Photosensitivity and RBC fluorescence under microscope
basis: Protoporphyrin accumulates in plasma and RBCs
diagnosis: Raised protoporphyrin levels in plasma, RBCs, and feces
treatment: Avoidance of sunlight and protective measures

defect: Ornithine transporter protein (ORNT1) failure to import ornithine into mitochondria
keyFeature: Hyperornithinemia, Hyperammonemia, and Homocitrullinuria (HHH triad)
basis: Without mitochondrial ornithine, urea cycle stalls; lysine carbamoylated instead → homocitrulline
diagnosis: Elevated plasma ornithine and ammonia; homocitrulline in urine
treatment: Low-protein diet and arginine supplementation

keyFeature: AIP-like abdominal pain and neuropathy PLUS photosensitivity
basis: Accumulation of coproporphyrin precursors
diagnosis: Uroporphyrins and coproporphyrins excreted in both urine and feces
treatment: High carbohydrate diet; avoidance of porphyrinogenic triggers

defect: ALA dehydratase (PBG synthase) - also inhibited by lead
keyFeature: Acute abdominal pain and neuropathy; also acquired via lead poisoning
basis: Block in second step of heme synthesis → high ALA levels are neurotoxic
diagnosis: Markedly increased plasma and urine ALA; decreased ALAD activity in RBCs
treatment: Supportive care; lead source removal if acquired

defect: A deficiency in the erythroid-specific enzyme ALA synthase (ALAS2) or the inhibition of ferrochelatase
keyFeature: Presence of ring sideroblasts in bone marrow examination
basis: When terminal steps of heme synthesis are blocked, iron cannot be incorporated into protoporphyrin ring, leading to accumulation of iron-laden mitochondria around the nucleus of RBC precursors
diagnosis: Bone marrow aspiration showing ring sideroblasts; genetic testing for ALAS2 mutation
treatment: High-dose pyridoxine (Vitamin B6); remove causative agent (e.g. lead) in acquired cases

keyFeature: Mixed porphyria with acute neurovisceral attacks and photosensitive cutaneous lesions
basis: Enzyme block causes accumulation of protoporphyrinogen IX, which oxidizes to protoporphyrin; in skin this triggers inflammatory reaction upon sun exposure
diagnosis: Demonstration of specific enzyme deficiency in erythrocytes or skin fibroblasts; increased protoporphyrin in feces
treatment: Avoid triggers (barbiturates, alcohol); high carbohydrate diet to suppress pathway; topical treatment for skin lesions

defect: Point mutation in β-globin: Glu→Val at position 6
keyFeature: Vaso-occlusive pain crises, hand-foot syndrome (dactylitis), and splenomegaly
basis: Deoxygenated HbS polymerises into fibres → RBCs sickle → clogs capillaries and ruptures
diagnosis: Hb electrophoresis (HbS band); positive sickling test with sodium dithionite
treatment: Hydration; pain management; hydroxyurea to increase HbF

defect: Absence or severe reduction of β-globin chain synthesis
keyFeature: 'Chipmunk facies' (frontal bossing), severe anemia, and hepatosplenomegaly
basis: Unbalanced alpha-chain accumulation → inclusion bodies damage RBC membrane → premature destruction
diagnosis: Nucleated RBCs on smear; microcytic hypochromic anemia; Hb electrophoresis showing absent HbA
treatment: Regular blood transfusions; iron chelation therapy to prevent iron overload

defect: Heterozygous state for β-thalassemia (one normal, one mutated gene)
keyFeature: Usually asymptomatic or mild anemia
basis: Moderate reduction in β-chain synthesis but sufficient for near-normal function
diagnosis: Mild microcytic hypochromic anemia; elevated HbA2 (>3.5%)
treatment: Usually no specific treatment required

keyFeature: Acute hemolytic anemia triggered by oxidant drugs (e.g., primaquine), fava beans, or infections
basis: Low NADPH prevents regeneration of reduced glutathione → RBCs vulnerable to oxidative lysis
diagnosis: Low G6PD activity on RBC enzyme assay; Heinz bodies
treatment: Avoidance of oxidant triggers and fava beans

defect: Met-Hb reductase deficiency (congenital) or oxidant drug exposure (acquired)
keyFeature: Cyanosis (bluish skin) and chocolate-coloured blood
basis: Iron in heme oxidised to ferric Fe³⁺ state - cannot bind or transport oxygen
diagnosis: Absorption peak at 633 nm; blood fails to turn red on shaking with air
treatment: IV methylene blue or oral Vitamin C

keyFeature: Chronic non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia
basis: Inadequate ATP production → RBC membrane failure and premature destruction in the spleen
diagnosis: High levels of 2,3-BPG; decreased oxygen affinity
treatment: Symptomatic management; splenectomy may be beneficial

defect: Dietary lack of retinol or beta-carotene
keyFeature: Night blindness (nyctalopia), Bitot's spots, and keratomalacia
basis: Deficiency of retinal prevents regeneration of rhodopsin in rod cells
diagnosis: Dark adaptation test; low serum Vitamin A
treatment: Vitamin A supplementation

defect: Lack of calcitriol due to poor diet or inadequate sunlight
keyFeature: Bow legs (genu varum), rickety rosary, and delayed suture closure in children
basis: Low Vitamin D → impaired mineralisation of newly formed bone matrix at growth plate
diagnosis: Low serum calcium and phosphate; high alkaline phosphatase (ALP)
treatment: Oral Vitamin D and calcium supplementation

keyFeature: Soft bones, frequent fractures, and bone pain
basis: Demineralisation of existing bones → increased fragility
diagnosis: Characteristic radiographic changes; low serum calcium
treatment: Vitamin D and calcium supplementation

keyFeature: Hemolytic anemia and neurological dysfunction
basis: Lack of Vitamin E (antioxidant) → peroxidation of PUFAs in RBC membranes
diagnosis: Low serum Vitamin E levels
treatment: Vitamin E supplementation

keyFeature: Bleeding tendencies and hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
basis: Deficiency prevents post-translational modification of Factors II, VII, IX, and X → cannot bind calcium
diagnosis: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and clotting time (CT)
treatment: Vitamin K administration

defect: Lack of Vitamin B1 (thiamine pyrophosphate - TPP)
keyFeature: Wet beriberi (cardiac failure) or dry beriberi (peripheral neuritis)
basis: Low TPP impairs energy production from carbohydrates - primarily affects heart and nerves
diagnosis: Decreased erythrocyte transketolase activity
treatment: Thiamine administration

pathway: Redox reactions using FMN and FAD
keyFeature: Angular stomatitis, cheilosis, and glossitis
basis: Impaired function of flavoproteins in the respiratory chain
diagnosis: Erythrocyte glutathione reductase activity test
treatment: Riboflavin supplementation

defect: Lack of Vitamin B3 or its precursor tryptophan
keyFeature: The 3 Ds - Dermatitis (Casal necklace), Diarrhea, and Dementia
basis: Deficiency of NAD/NADP coenzymes needed for widespread metabolic redox reactions
diagnosis: Clinical signs; urinary N-methylnicotinamide measurement
treatment: Oral nicotinamide supplementation

defect: Lack of Vitamin B6 (PLP); often drug-induced (isoniazid/INH)
keyFeature: Peripheral neuritis, convulsions in children, and sideroblastic anemia
basis: Failure of PLP-dependent enzymes - GABA synthesis (convulsions) and heme synthesis (anemia)
diagnosis: High urinary xanthurenic acid after tryptophan load
treatment: Pyridoxine supplementation

keyFeature: Macrocytic anemia and neural tube defects in pregnancy
basis: Impaired DNA synthesis due to lack of dTMP production → arrest of cell division in bone marrow
diagnosis: High urinary FIGLU excretion after histidine load
treatment: Folic acid supplementation

defect: Lack of cobalamin or intrinsic factor (pernicious anemia)
pathway: One-carbon metabolism and fatty acid catabolism
keyFeature: Megaloblastic anemia and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord
basis: Folate trap prevents DNA synthesis; methylmalonyl-CoA accumulation causes demyelination
diagnosis: Low serum B12; Schilling test; hypersegmented neutrophils on blood smear
treatment: Intramuscular Vitamin B12 injections

defect: Dietary lack or chronic blood loss
keyFeature: Microcytic hypochromic anemia, easy fatiguability, and apathy
basis: Deficient iron stops incorporation of iron into protoporphyrin to form heme
diagnosis: Low serum ferritin; high total iron binding capacity (TIBC)
treatment: Oral ferrous salts with Vitamin C

defect: Acquired iron overload (Bantu siderosis or excessive blood transfusions)
keyFeature: Brown discoloration of skin and organ damage
basis: Hemosiderin accumulates in tissues when ferritin storage capacity is exceeded
diagnosis: High serum iron; ferritin >1000 ng/ml
treatment: Repeated phlebotomy or iron chelators (desferrioxamine)

defect: Hereditary defect in HFE gene → excessive iron absorption
keyFeature: 'Bronze diabetes' - cirrhosis, hyperpigmentation, and diabetes mellitus
basis: Progressive iron deposition causes oxidative damage and cell death in liver, pancreas, and skin
diagnosis: Liver biopsy showing siderosis; genetic testing for HFE mutations
treatment: Lifelong periodic phlebotomy

keyFeature: Kayser-Fleischer (KF) rings in eye, tremors, and liver cirrhosis
basis: Failure to excrete copper into bile → toxic accumulation in brain and liver
diagnosis: Low serum ceruloplasmin; high 24-hr urinary copper
treatment: Copper chelators (D-penicillamine); low-copper diet

keyFeature: 'Kinky' steely hair, hypothermia, and developmental delay
basis: Copper trapped in intestinal cells → cannot reach blood → systemic copper deficiency
diagnosis: Twisted hair (pili torti) on microscopy; low serum copper
treatment: Injections of copper salts (limited efficacy)

keyFeature: Periorificial dermatitis, diarrhea, and alopecia
basis: Zinc is a cofactor for >300 enzymes; deficiency impairs wound healing and immunity
diagnosis: Very low serum zinc levels
treatment: High-dose oral zinc supplementation

keyFeature: Goiter (thyroid enlargement) and hypothyroidism
basis: Low iodine prevents T3/T4 synthesis → compensatory TSH rise → gland hyperplasia
diagnosis: Low serum T4; high TSH
treatment: Iodized salt and iodine supplementation

defect: Excessive fluoride intake (>2 ppm in water)
keyFeature: Mottled enamel and chalky white patches on teeth
basis: High fluoride disrupts enamel formation; increases bone density inappropriately (skeletal fluorosis)
diagnosis: Dental examination; skeletal X-rays showing increased density
treatment: Changing to a safe water source

keyFeature: Endemic dilated cardiomyopathy
basis: Selenium is a component of glutathione peroxidase; deficiency → oxidative heart damage
diagnosis: Very low serum selenium (<70 ng/ml)
treatment: Selenium supplementation

keyFeature: Bleeding gums, loose teeth, and perifollicular hemorrhages
basis: Inability to hydroxylate proline and lysine → structurally weak collagen and fragile blood vessels
diagnosis: Low serum ascorbic acid levels
treatment: Vitamin C supplements and fresh fruits

defect: Low ionised calcium levels in blood
keyFeature: Carpopedal spasm (adduction of thumb) and Chvostek sign
basis: Low calcium lowers the threshold for nerve excitation → spontaneous muscle contractions
diagnosis: Serum calcium <7 mg/dl; positive Trousseau sign
treatment: IV calcium gluconate and oral Vitamin D

keyFeature: Hepatosplenomegaly, bone erosion (Erlenmeyer flask deformity), and anemia
basis: Glucocerebroside accumulates in reticuloendothelial cells → 'wrinkled paper' macrophages
diagnosis: Bone marrow biopsy showing Gaucher cells; β-glucosidase enzyme assay
treatment: Enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)

keyFeature: Hepatosplenomegaly, cherry red spot on macula, and severe neurodegeneration
basis: Sphingomyelin and cholesterol accumulate in lysosomes of macrophages ('foam cells') in liver, spleen, and brain
diagnosis: Bone marrow biopsy (Niemann-Pick foam cells); sphingomyelinase enzyme assay in WBCs
treatment: No definitive treatment; ERT in clinical trials

keyFeature: Cherry red spot on retina, mental retardation, microcephaly, and seizures
basis: Failure to degrade GM2 ganglioside → toxic accumulation in neurocytes and retinal ganglion cells
diagnosis: Decreased β-hexosaminidase A in blood; ophthalmoscopic fundus examination
treatment: Symptomatic management; ERT and gene therapy under trial

keyFeature: Purplish skin papules (angiokeratomas), progressive renal failure, and painful crises
basis: Ceramide trihexoside (globotriaosylceramide) accumulates primarily in kidneys and vascular endothelium
diagnosis: Accumulated lipid in tissues; α-galactosidase enzyme assay
treatment: Enzyme replacement therapy

keyFeature: Severe mental retardation, total CNS demyelination, and 'globoid bodies' in white matter
basis: Galactocerebroside accumulates - inability to cleave into ceramide and galactose
diagnosis: Globoid bodies in brain tissue on histology; enzyme assay
treatment: Symptomatic support

keyFeature: Demyelination, neurological deficit, and optic atrophy
basis: Sulfogalactocerebroside (sulfatides) accumulate in most tissues - particularly myelin sheaths
diagnosis: Arylsulfatase A deficiency in tissues or urine
treatment: Supportive care

keyFeature: Corneal clouding, skeletal deformities (dysostosis multiplex), and coarse facial features
basis: Lysosomal accumulation of heparan sulfate (HS) and dermatan sulfate (DS) in heart, brain, and joints
diagnosis: High HS/DS in urine; absent α-L-iduronidase in fibroblasts
treatment: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and ERT

keyFeature: Clear cornea (unlike Hurler), deafness, joint stiffness
basis: HS and DS accumulate in various tissues
diagnosis: HS/DS in urine; deficient iduronate-2-sulfatase activity
treatment: ERT and multidisciplinary supportive therapy

defect: Lysosomal acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase) - also a GSD
keyFeature: Massive cardiomegaly, severe hypotonia ('floppy infant'), and cardiac failure
basis: Only GSD that is also a lysosomal storage disorder; glycogen accumulates in lysosomes of heart and skeletal muscle
diagnosis: Acid maltase assay in dried blood spot/fibroblasts; glycogen-laden lysosomes on muscle biopsy
treatment: Recombinant ERT (α-glucosidase)

defect: Heparan sulphamidase (Type A) or N-acetyl-glucosaminidase (Type B)
keyFeature: Hyperactivity, profound intellectual deterioration, and mild somatic changes
basis: Progressive lysosomal accumulation of heparan sulfate primarily affecting the CNS
diagnosis: High urinary heparan sulfate; specific enzyme assays
treatment: Symptomatic management

defect: Galactose-6-sulfate sulfatase (Type A) or β-galactosidase (Type B)
keyFeature: Short stature, motor dysfunction, and epiphyseal dysplasia
basis: Keratan sulfate (KS) and chondroitin sulfate (CS) accumulate in bones and cornea
diagnosis: KS and CS in urine; skeletal radiographic findings
treatment: Orthopedic and respiratory support

keyFeature: Severe skeletal deformity, heart defects, and normal intelligence
basis: Selective accumulation of dermatan sulfate (DS) in connective tissues
diagnosis: High DS in urine; specific enzyme assay
treatment: ERT and surgical management of skeletal issues

defect: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the basal ganglia
keyFeature: Mask-like face, resting tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia
basis: Severely decreased dopamine levels; presence of Lewy bodies (alpha-synuclein deposits)
diagnosis: Clinical signs and response to dopaminergic medication
treatment: L-DOPA and carbidopa

defect: Misfolding and deposition of amyloid-β and tau proteins
keyFeature: Progressive memory loss, dementia, and cognitive decline
basis: Extracellular senile plaques (amyloid-β) and neurofibrillary tangles (tau) → neuronal death and loss of acetylcholine
diagnosis: Clinical assessment; MRI brain atrophy; Aβ and tau markers
treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors; anti-inflammatory drugs

defect: Severe protein deficiency with adequate or marginal calorie intake
keyFeature: Pitting edema, 'flag sign' hair, and protuberant abdomen
basis: Hypoalbuminemia (causing edema) and decreased apoprotein synthesis (causing fatty liver)
diagnosis: Low serum albumin and clinical appearance
treatment: Balanced protein-rich diet administered gradually

defect: Deficiency of both total calories and protein
keyFeature: Generalized wasting, absence of subcutaneous fat, and dry skin
basis: Body utilises structural proteins and fat for energy due to extreme starvation → 'skin and bone' appearance
diagnosis: Clinical examination (child appears like an old man)
treatment: Gradual refeeding and calorie supplementation

keyFeature: Lack of pigment in skin, hair, and iris; photophobia; and sun sensitivity
basis: Inability to convert tyrosine to melanin → no UV protection for skin and eyes
diagnosis: Clinical observation of generalised hypopigmentation
treatment: Sun protection (sunscreen, sunglasses); monitoring for skin cancers

defect: Congenital thyroid hormone deficiency (often from maternal iodine deficiency)
keyFeature: Stunted growth, mental retardation, and coarse facial features
basis: Low T3/T4 during critical development impairs CNS maturation and bone growth
diagnosis: Newborn screening: low T4 and high TSH
treatment: Life-long thyroxine (T4) administration

keyFeature: Enlargement of the thyroid gland
basis: Low iodine → low T3/T4 → compensatory TSH rise → hyperplasia and hypertrophy of thyroid gland
diagnosis: Examination and palpation of neck; low urinary iodine
treatment: Iodized salt and iodine supplementation

defect: Excessive Growth Hormone (GH) secretion in adults
keyFeature: Enlarged hands, feet, facial bones, and prognathism
basis: GH excess after epiphyseal closure → overgrowth of soft tissues and membrane bones
diagnosis: High serum GH and IGF-1; lack of GH suppression after glucose load
treatment: Surgical removal of pituitary tumour or somatostatin analogs

keyFeature: Moon face, buffalo hump, abdominal striae, and hypertension
basis: Prolonged hypercortisolism → increased gluconeogenesis, fat redistribution, and protein wasting
diagnosis: High 24-hr urinary free cortisol; dexamethasone suppression test
treatment: Removal of adrenal/pituitary tumour or cortisol-inhibiting drugs

keyFeature: Skin hyperpigmentation (bronzing), hypotension, and weight loss
basis: Deficiency of cortisol and aldosterone → increased ACTH (stimulates melanocytes) and sodium wasting
diagnosis: Low serum cortisol and aldosterone; high plasma ACTH
treatment: Life-long glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement

defect: Drug-induced displacement of bilirubin from albumin binding sites
keyFeature: Sudden onset jaundice or kernicterus risk in infants
basis: Phenylbutazone competes with bilirubin for albumin; displaced free bilirubin crosses the blood-brain barrier
diagnosis: Drug history; high indirect (unconjugated) bilirubin
treatment: Discontinuation of drug; phototherapy if needed

defect: Transient UDP-glucuronosyltransferase deficiency or Rh/ABO incompatibility
keyFeature: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera in first week of life
basis: Immature liver cannot conjugate bilirubin fast enough → unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
diagnosis: Serum total and indirect bilirubin levels
treatment: Phototherapy (isomerises bilirubin to soluble forms) or exchange transfusion

keyFeature: Severe jaundice from birth; unconjugated bilirubin 20-45 mg/dl; kernicterus
basis: Absolute inability to conjugate bilirubin → life-threatening neurotoxicity
diagnosis: Extreme unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; NO response to phenobarbital
treatment: Vigorous phototherapy; liver transplantation

defect: Severe partial deficiency of bilirubin-UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (~10% activity)
keyFeature: Milder jaundice than Type I; unconjugated bilirubin <20 mg/dl; fewer neurological signs
basis: Reduced but present enzyme activity allows some bilirubin conjugation
diagnosis: Partial RESPONSE to phenobarbital (which induces the enzyme)
treatment: Phenobarbital therapy

defect: Mild deficiency of bilirubin-UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (~33% activity retained)
keyFeature: Transient mild jaundice triggered by stress, fasting, or illness
basis: Reduced bilirubin clearance → mild rise in unconjugated bilirubin (<4 mg/dl)
diagnosis: Mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes
treatment: Usually none required; phenobarbital if necessary

keyFeature: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and black-coloured liver
basis: Defective secretion of conjugated bilirubin from hepatocytes into bile canaliculi → retrograde leak into blood
diagnosis: Liver biopsy showing dark pigment; secondary peak in BSP excretion test
treatment: Symptomatic care; prognosis excellent

keyFeature: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia WITHOUT black liver pigmentation
basis: Failure of liver to re-uptake conjugated bilirubin → elevation in blood
diagnosis: Conjugated jaundice; NORMAL BSP excretion curve (unlike Dubin-Johnson)
treatment: Supportive care

defect: Imbalance between gastric acid aggression and mucosal defense, often associated with excessive gastric acid secretion
pathway: Gastric acid secretion pathway mediated by H2 histamine receptors in the stomach
keyFeature: Vague abdominal pain; severe cases may manifest as hematemesis or hemorrhage leading to anemia
basis: Histamine acts on H2 receptors of gastric parietal cells to stimulate hydrochloric acid (HCl) secretion
diagnosis: Clinical history; tubeless gastric analysis using Azure-A dye-bound resin
treatment: H2 receptor antagonists such as cimetidine

defect: Inhibition of Cytochrome oxidase a3 in the ETC
keyFeature: Sudden collapse, almond breath odour, and high anion gap metabolic acidosis
basis: Cyanide binds Fe³⁺ of cytochrome oxidase → stops ATP production → cellular hypoxia
diagnosis: Clinical history; elevated blood cyanide; high anion gap
treatment: Amyl nitrite; sodium thiosulfate; hydroxocobalamin

keyFeature: Cherry-red discoloration of blood and skin; severe hypoxia
basis: CO has 200ÃÂ higher affinity for Hb than O₂ → O₂ displaced; ODC shifted left → impaired O₂ delivery
diagnosis: COHb levels measured by co-oximetry
treatment: 100% oxygen or hyperbaric oxygen

defect: Inhibition of ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase by lead
keyFeature: Abdominal colic, irritability, anemia, and wrist drop
basis: Lead binds thiol groups → blocks heme synthesis → ALA accumulates - neurotoxic
diagnosis: Basophilic stippling of RBCs; ring sideroblasts; high urinary ALA and blood lead
treatment: Lead source removal; chelation therapy (EDTA, dimercaprol)

defect: Inhibition of thiol-containing enzymes by mercury
keyFeature: Minamata disease: neurological damage, tremors, and visual field constriction
basis: Mercury has high affinity for sulfhydryl (-SH) groups → widespread inactivation of cellular enzymes
diagnosis: Mercury levels in blood or hair
treatment: Chelation with dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA)

keyFeature: Miosis (pinpoint pupils), excessive salivation, muscle fasciculations, and respiratory failure
basis: Organophosphates phosphorylate the active site → toxic buildup of acetylcholine at nerve endings
diagnosis: Serum cholinesterase activity levels
treatment: Atropine and pralidoxime (2-PAM)

defect: Alcohol dehydrogenase converts methanol to formic acid
keyFeature: Sudden blindness and severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis
basis: Formic acid inhibits mitochondrial respiration - specifically damages the optic nerve
diagnosis: History of illicit alcohol; high osmolal gap; metabolic acidosis
treatment: IV ethanol or fomepizole (competitive inhibitor); dialysis

keyFeature: Acute renal failure and severe metabolic acidosis
basis: Oxalic acid forms calcium oxalate crystals that precipitate in renal tubules → obstructive damage
diagnosis: Envelope-shaped oxalate crystals in urine; metabolic acidosis
treatment: Ethanol or fomepizole to block metabolism; dialysis

defect: GlcNAc-phosphotransferase (lysosomal enzyme targeting defect - Golgi apparatus)
keyFeature: Severe psychomotor retardation, coarse facies, and 'I-cells' (inclusion bodies)
basis: Absence of mannose-6-phosphate tagging prevents enzymes from reaching lysosomes → secreted into plasma instead
diagnosis: Low lysosomal enzymes in cells but unusually high level in plasma
treatment: Symptomatic management

defect: Mitochondrial DNA point mutations in Complex I subunits
keyFeature: Sudden-onset bilateral loss of central vision in young adult males
basis: Mitochondrial energy production impaired → focal degeneration of retinal ganglion cell layer and optic nerve
diagnosis: Tortuous retinal vessels on ophthalmoscopy; mtDNA mutation analysis
treatment: Symptomatic; gene therapy under trial

keyFeature: Bone pain, renal failure, and Bence Jones proteinuria
basis: Monoclonal light chains damage organs; characteristic 'M-band' on electrophoresis
diagnosis: M-band on electrophoresis; Bradshaw's test for urine light chains; bone marrow biopsy
treatment: Chemotherapy; stem cell transplantation

defect: Obstruction of biliary tract by stones in the gallbladder or bile ducts
keyFeature: Obstructive jaundice with yellowish discoloration, clay-colored stools, dark high-colored urine
basis: Stone prevents conjugated bilirubin from reaching intestinal lumen; urobilinogen is not formed by gut bacteria, leading to loss of normal fecal color
diagnosis: Negative urinary urobilinogen, positive urinary bile pigments/salts, palpable gallbladder
treatment: Surgical intervention to remove stones and relieve obstruction
